questions.text: When the polynomial 3x⁴ + px³ – 7x + 5 is divided by x – 1, the remainder is 10. Find p.
Solve x² – 6kx = 5k² for x, in terms of k.
Prove that (kx)² = 7 – x/k has real roots for all real values of k, where k ≠ 0.
questions.markingGuide: k²x² + x/k – 7 = 0. Disc = 1/k² + 28k². Since k≠0, both terms positive. Disc > 0. Roots always real.

questions.text: Solve z³ + 8m³i = 0 in polar form, in terms of m (m > 0).

The locus |z – 5i| – |z + 5i| = 8.

Find the Cartesian equation in the form ay² – bx² = k.
Given u = 4 + i and w = –2 – 5i, find z = 2u + 3w.
If u = m cis(2π/3), write u³ in the form a + bi, in terms of m.
If (g + i)(3 + hi) = (7 + i)(2 – i), find all possible values of g and h (real).
questions.markingGuide: RHS: (7+i)(2–i) = 14–7i+2i–i² = 15–5i. LHS: (g+i)(3+hi) = (3g–h)+(gh+3)i. Real: 3g–h = 15. Imag: gh+3 = –5, gh = –8. From first: h = 3g–15. Substitute: g(3g–15) = –8. 3g²–15g+8 = 0. Disc = 225–96 = 129. Not clean. Use (g+2i)(1+hi)=(4+i)(3–2i). RHS: 12–8i+3i–2i²=14–5i. 1·g–2h+(gh+2)i=14–5i. g–2h=14, gh+2=–5 → gh=–7. h=(g–14)/2. g(g–14)/2=–7. g²–14g+14=0. Disc=196–56=140. Still messy. Keep simple: g=1, h=–12 and g=4, h=–3 would need: 3(1)–(–12)=15 ✓, 1(–12)+3=–9≠–5 ✗. OK this approach needs rethinking. Use direct: 3g–h=15, gh=–8. h=3g–15. g(3g–15)=–8. 3g²–15g+8=0. g=(15±√129)/6. These are irrational. Accept irrational solutions.

questions.text: Given that arg((d + 6i)/(1 – di)) = π/4, find d (real).
One solution of a quadratic equation with real coefficients is x = 4 + √(3p)i. Find the equation in terms of p.
questions.markingGuide: Other root: 4–√(3p)i. Sum=8, Product=16+3p. Equation: x²–8x+16+3p=0.

questions.text: Expand and simplify (√(3a) – √(5a)i)², in terms of a.
One solution of 2z³ + pz² + qz – 10 = 0 is z = 1 + 2i. If p, q are real, find the other solutions and p, q.
questions.expectedAnswer: p = –6, q = 14; other solutions z = 1–2i and z = 1
questions.markingGuide: z=1–2i also a root. Factor: z²–2z+5. f(z)=2(z²–2z+5)(z–a). Constant: 2(5)(–a)=–10. a=1. Expand: 2(z³–z²–2z²+2z+5z–5)=2(z³–3z²+7z–5)=2z³–6z²+14z–10. p=–6, q=14. Third root z=1.
